lemma: L1 (reformulation of 40a). Let M range over the uniform one-pass class of 40a. (i) Logical negation: NOT(40a) <=> exists M, c, d, m0 such that for all m >= m0: S_M(m) <= s(m)^c AND tau_M(m) <= s(m)^d. Proof: negate the prefix of 40a (forall M, forall c,d, forall m0, exists m>=m0 : S>s^c or tau>s^d) by de Morgan. (ii) Eventual versus all-length bounds: if such an M has the bounds only for m >= m0, define M' that runs M for m >= m0 and, for the finitely many m < m0, uses a fixed table of answers; for each fixed m < m0 the table has constant size (it depends only on m0 and s), so S_M'(m) <= s(m)^c' and tau_M'(m) <= s(m)^d' for all m with suitable constants c', d' (absorb the constant table into the polynomial via s(m) >= m). Hence 40a is equivalent to the 'all sufficiently large m' form of the MMW hypothesis that no poly-space, poly-update-time one-pass algorithm solves exact total Search-MCSP^A[s]. Caveat for (ii): this needs s(m) >= m and the table size to be bounded by a constant independent of the machine's own s-dependence; I checked the case form only, not the uniformity conditions of [4].
gap: G0001 (open, unchanged): a lower bound showing that for admissible s, A in PH, every uniform deterministic one-pass machine for exact total Search-MCSP^A[s] has, for infinitely many m, space > s^c or worst-case update time > s^d. L1 only restates it. This is the update-time lower bound the manuscript's own section 8 calls not established, and it is the premise Q-156fa9c912 / Q-9c4d56f01f list as open. No computation at this level of abstraction can decide it, and no barrier-passing construction is yet in hand. lemma: L1 corrected. For (40a) the finite-length absorption holds: for m >= 2, s(m) >= m >= 2 (time-constructible s(n) >= n), so for any finite set of exceptional lengths m < m0 a fixed lookup table costs a constant depending only on m0, and a suitable exponent c covers it. Hence eventual-bound and all-length forms are equivalent for uniform one-pass machines. This is a reformulation only and closes no obligation.
